expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: Caps and repetition don't change that; one time in ten is exactly what an instruction-only rule looks like.

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: The fix is to move both rules from prose to a device that refuses the call before it runs.

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Provides deny block with Bash(git push --force:*), Bash(git push -f:*), Edit/Write/MultiEdit(./src/generated/**)

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: Deny strings match the **prefix** of a command...slip past. That rule needs a `PreToolUse` hook that inspects the command.

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: Every message must say what was blocked, why, and what to do instead.

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Section 5 'Prove it fires — don't skip this': Ask Claude to git push --force and to edit a file in src/generated/, then confirm git push --force-with-lease still works.

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: .claude/settings.json, committed. A rule in settings.local.json protects one laptop

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: Two rules, two mechanisms...rung 1...so it needs logic. No amount of emphasis moves prose up the ladder.
